title: Thermodynamics & Kinetics
syllabus: Introduction and terminologies; zeroth law, first law, enthalpy and heat capacity; applications of the first law; second law; Carnot cycle; third law and the Gibbs–Helmholtz equation; chemical kinetics (rate equation, order of the reaction, integral rate equations, half-life of reactions); collision theory, effect of temperature and catalysts on reaction rate; numericals.

syllabusRows.text: Introduction, terminologies
Zeroth law, first law, enthalpy and heat capacity
Applications of the first law, second law
Carnot cycle
Third law, Gibbs–Helmholtz equation
Chemical kinetics: rate equation, order of the reaction, integral rate equations, half-life of reactions
Collision theory, effect of temperature and catalysts on reaction rate
Numericals

title: Energy Devices
syllabus: Electrochemical and electrolytic cells, electrode materials with examples; Nernst equation and numericals; classification of batteries; chemistry of Li-ion secondary batteries; fuel cells (H₂–O₂ and solid oxide); solar cells (silicon photovoltaic cell); photoelectrochemical cells; dye-sensitized cells.

syllabusRows.text: Electrochemical and electrolytic cells, electrode materials with examples; Nernst equation and numericals
Classification of batteries
Chemistry of Li-ion secondary batteries
Fuel cells: H₂–O₂ and solid oxide
Solar cells: silicon photovoltaic cell
Photoelectrochemical cells
Dye-sensitized solar cells

title: Functional Materials
syllabus: Electrical materials (Ohm’s law and resistivity); classification of metals and semiconductors; intrinsic and extrinsic Si, insulators, superconductors; magnetic materials (para and dia, ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic and applications in storage devices); liquid cooling (types of coolants, thermal conductivity and applications); nanomaterials (introduction, top-down and bottom-up approaches for synthesis, bulk vs nano gold, quantum dots).

syllabusRows.text: Electrical materials: Ohm’s law and resistivity
Classification of metals and semiconductors
Intrinsic and extrinsic Si, insulators, superconductors
Magnetic materials: para- and diamagnetic, ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic; applications in storage devices
Liquid cooling: types of coolants, thermal conductivity and applications
Nanomaterials: introduction
Top-down and bottom-up approaches for synthesis
Bulk vs nano gold, quantum dots

title: Spectroscopy & Diffraction
syllabus: Fundamental concepts in spectroscopic and diffraction techniques; principle and instrumentation of UV-Visible spectroscopy; applications of UV-Visible; powder XRD, determination of crystallite size, numericals.

syllabusRows.text: Fundamental concepts in spectroscopic techniques
Fundamental concepts in diffraction techniques
UV-Visible spectroscopy: principle, instrumentation and applications
Powder XRD: determination of crystallite size, numericals

title: Computational Chemistry
syllabus: Introduction to quantum mechanical calculations; molecular orbital theory (atomic orbitals, molecular orbitals); orbital interactions and chemical bonding; potential energy curve and surface; electrostatic potentials; geometry optimisation; frequency; reaction mechanism; application of AI to screen semiconductors.
